stories.title: 216M Spy TVs – The LG Smart TV Problem [video]
stories.blurb: LG's smart TVs are shipping with ACR (Automatic Content Recognition) surveillance baked in, tracking what 216 million households watch and reporting home. A deep dive video exposé with 933 comments worth of rage — this is the canonical reference for why you should never connect a TV to Wi-Fi. If you own an LG set, this one's required viewing.

stories.title: Mistral raises €3B
stories.blurb: Mistral just closed a monster €3B round while doubling down on sovereign, open-weight frontier models — a direct challenge to the closed-source hegemony of OpenAI and Anthropic. The framing around "sovereign AI" matters enormously for European enterprises and anyone who cares about running models they actually control. Watch this space.

stories.title: Jellyfin 12.0
stories.blurb: The open-source, zero-tracking Plex alternative lands its biggest release yet with Jellyfin 12.0. Major UI overhaul, improved hardware transcoding, and a slew of long-requested features — this is the privacy-respecting media server that just keeps getting better.

stories.title: I've factored the RSA keys of a Certificate Authority from the 90s
stories.blurb: A researcher cracked a legacy 90s CA's RSA keys, laying bare exactly how badly ancient PKI infrastructure has aged. It's a practical reminder that the internet's trust chain has rotting timbers — and a gripping technical detective story of how weak key generation compounds over decades.

stories.title: We have a year to fix security everywhere
stories.blurb: A rallying cry from the Rust security ecosystem arguing we have roughly one year before systemic supply-chain attacks become unmanageable. Concrete proposals for hardening the open-source toolchain, and the comment thread is unusually substantive. Share this with your security-adjacent colleagues.

stories.title: TALA Is Open-Source
stories.blurb: TALA, the best automatic layout engine for D2 diagrams, just went open-source. If you've ever wrestled with Graphviz's chaotic layouts or paid for diagramming tools, this is the unlock you've been waiting for — clean, hierarchical graph layout free as in beer and freedom.

stories.title: There's a new "Google Jail" for independent wikis
stories.blurb: The RuneScape wiki crew documents how Google is systematically burying independent wikis in search results, effectively handing a monopoly to Fandom and its ad-bloated clones. A chilling first-person account of how algorithmic penalties can kill a community-maintained knowledge base overnight.

stories.title: Trusting-Trust Attack against an Entire Linux Distribution
stories.blurb: Researchers demonstrate a Ken Thompson-style "trusting trust" compiler backdoor attack scaled to an entire Linux distro — not just a compiler, but the whole reproducible-build chain. This is the kind of supply-chain nightmare that keeps infosec people awake at 3am, and now it's peer-reviewed.

stories.title: How well do agents use test/verification techniques?
stories.blurb: Dan Luu systematically evaluates whether coding agents actually leverage tests and formal verification to self-check their output — spoiler: they mostly don't, and the failure modes are instructive. Essential reading if you're using Claude Code or any agentic coding tool in production.

stories.title: The VMs Powering Mobile Agents (Instinct, Claude Code)
stories.blurb: A technical deep-dive into the sandboxed VM infrastructure that powers mobile and agentic AI systems like Claude Code — covering isolation models, execution environments, and the tradeoffs between security and capability. If you build with or on top of agentic tools, this is the behind-the-curtain look you didn't know you needed.

stories.title: redhat-et/ripwire: The ripgrep of AI context
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: llms, tolearn, totry, tohomebrew, embeddings, via:twitter, via:agenticgirl, mymisunderstandingisnowreal
stories.blurb: Red Hat Emerging Technologies drops a zero-dependency C++23 binary that maps your entire codebase structurally — no embeddings, no vector DB, no daemon — and hands coding agents precisely the symbols, callers, and blast radius they need for a given task. This is a fundamentally smarter approach to repo context than RAG, and it's installable via Homebrew today.

stories.title: VMs won't contain cyber-capable agents - The Trail of Bits Blog
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, security, vm
stories.blurb: Trail of Bits argues convincingly that traditional VM-based sandboxing is not a viable containment strategy for AI agents with offensive cyber capabilities. As agentic AI becomes more capable, the security assumptions baked into current deployment architectures are dangerously naive — this is the paper that should be influencing every AI safety conversation.

stories.title: Recordly - Open-source app for incredible screen recordings.
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: screenshot, video, demo
stories.blurb: Recordly is an open-source screen recorder that adds auto-zoom, smooth cursor animations, and cinematic polish to your recordings automatically. A gorgeous alternative to the pricey Rotato/Screen Studio crowd — if you make dev demos or tutorials, try this before paying for anything else.

stories.title: TMOG — Native Task Manager for macOS and Windows
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: mac, apple, software, lukas-zuzanak
stories.blurb: TMOG is a native, lightweight task manager for macOS that eschews the bloat of Notion and Things in favor of clarity and speed. Built specifically for the Apple ecosystem with a clean interface — exactly the kind of focused utility that Pinboard surfaces and App Store charts miss.

stories.title: I'm done using AI – Brett Codes
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: llm, coding, firsthand, 2026
stories.blurb: A developer's candid first-hand account of stepping back from AI coding tools after months of heavy use — documenting where the productivity gains evaporated and what it cost him in understanding and craft. Counterpoint to the hype cycle, and worth reading even if you disagree with the conclusion.

stories.title: GitHub - scastiel/kado: Kadō — A privacy-first habit tracker for iPhone and iPad.
stories.blurb: Kadō is an open-source, privacy-first habit tracker for iPhone and iPad — no accounts, no cloud sync, no tracking. The source is on GitHub, so you can audit exactly what it does with your data. A rare example of a native iOS app that actually walks the privacy talk.

stories.title: The best dark mode toggle is probably none • Lea Verou
stories.blurb: CSS luminary Lea Verou makes the counterintuitive case that the optimal dark mode implementation respects the OS-level system preference and ships no toggle at all. Loaded with practical CSS patterns and the kind of nuanced UX thinking that separates thoughtful engineers from checkbox-ticklers.

stories.title: Easy local Copilot with VS Code and Lemonade
stories.blurb: A step-by-step guide to wiring up a fully local AI code-completion setup in VS Code using Lemonade — no telemetry, no API keys, no monthly bill. If you've been meaning to ditch Copilot for an on-device alternative, this is the cleanest tutorial available right now.

stories.title: GitHub - genspark-ai/genoffice: Free, open-source alternative to Microsoft Office with built-in AI agents
stories.blurb: GenOffice is a free, open-source desktop suite handling Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF, and Markdown with AI agents baked in — targeting macOS, Windows, and Linux. Ambitious and early, but if it delivers on even half its promise, this could be a serious LibreOffice successor for the AI era.

stories.title: The car industry A/B tested selling a car with and without CarPlay and the results are not shocking
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: carplay, cars, 2020s, GM, honda, research, data, sales
stories.blurb: GM removed CarPlay from Chevy EVs in favor of Google's Android Automotive OS, and the market replied by buying the Honda badge-equivalent that still had CarPlay instead. Real sales data confirms what Apple ecosystem fans already knew: CarPlay is a purchasing decision, not a nice-to-have. A satisfying data-driven vindication.
